story_title: Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy SSL-VPN heap-based buffer overflow CVE-2023-27997 listed in the KEV catalog

provenance.note: Live end-to-end holdout v8 candidate (revision 2), matcher-limit demonstration. The official Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-23-097) states affected versions in prose branch ranges (FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.4, 7.0.0 through 7.0.11, and 6.4 branches; FortiProxy ranges) which the closed matcher grammar cannot parse; revision-4 semantics require such expressions to route to human review with an explicit unknown and never persist as an auto claim — the hard assertion is the global unsupported_claim counter, not the outcome set. KEV membership verified against the official CISA catalog feed on 2026-10-11 (catalogVersion 2026.10.08: Fortinet | FortiOS and FortiProxy SSL-VPN | added 2023-06-13). Disjoint from the development datasets and every consumed holdout v1-v7.

story_title: Microsoft Windows DNS Server remote code execution CVE-2020-1350 (SIGRed) listed in the KEV catalog; a superseded internal memo claimed builds 17763.1 and earlier were fixed

provenance.note: Live end-to-end holdout v8 candidate (revision 3 after the first review round), stale-version-rejection demonstration. The Story title deliberately carries a stale, evidence-free version sentence ('builds 17763.1 and earlier were fixed'); extraction never sees the title, and the runner's grounding detector fails any persisted claims row whose supported range expression does not appear verbatim in its cited evidence, so the stale build number must not surface in the record. Outcome set is quoting-robust; the hard guarantees are known_exploited=yes grounded in stored KEV evidence and the detector set. KEV membership verified against the official CISA catalog feed on 2026-10-11 (catalogVersion 2026.10.08: Microsoft | Windows | CVE-2020-1350 SIGRed, added 2021-11-03). Disjoint from the development datasets and every consumed holdout v1-v7.
